properties.description: Every presented data byte matches an already accepted ordered input prefix or a justified zero-padding byte.
Presented output last marks exactly the final retained or padded byte, independently of sink readiness.
Every presented status describes the next completed accepted frame, with correct original length, adjusted length, padding and truncation flags.
Data and status channels independently retain valid and payload while blocked; reset cancels these hold obligations.
Synchronous reset clears response valids and cancels epoch obligations; unknown meaningful response controls cannot establish success.

Combinational final-marker completion requires the development-length drain tail, no incomplete accepted input, no outstanding independent responses and no remaining valids. The check needs no subsequent clock edge.

request_count_semantics: Conservative explicit HTTP dispatch attempts;HTTP issuance/cost unknown on failures.

properties.description: P0: Every presented data beat is justified by an already accepted byte or known zero padding, in frame order, with the required final-byte marker; checks partial streaming prefixes without waiting for status.
P1: Every presented status describes the next completed accepted frame, including original length, clamped length and pad/truncate flags, independently of data-channel progress.
P2: A blocked data response retains valid, data and last until transfer or synchronous reset.
P3: A blocked status response retains valid and all status fields until transfer or synchronous reset.

P4: Reset clears response valids and cancels private epoch obligations without clearing previous alarms. Unknown meaningful observations and exceeded bounded tracking capacity never establish success.
P5: Combinational final-marker completion requires no remaining offered input, partial accepted frame, expected data or status, or presented response; no additional clock edge is needed.

request_count_semantics: Conservative explicit HTTP dispatch attempts;HTTP issuance/cost unknown on failures.

properties.description: Every presented data beat matches an already accepted ordered input prefix or justified zero padding, with the required last marker, independently of ready.
Every presented header matches the next completed accepted frame: original length, clamped length, padding and truncation; header progress is independent of data progress.
Blocked data retains valid, byte and last through subsequent observations until transfer or synchronous reset.
Blocked headers retain valid and all header fields until transfer or synchronous reset.
Reset clears response valids and cancels epoch obligations without erasing previous alarms. Unknown meaningful tracked observations and exceeded tracking bounds cannot establish success.

The final-post marker combinationally checks completion: no offered input, incomplete accepted frame, outstanding data/header obligations or presented responses remain. No additional edge is required.

properties.description: Every presented data byte matches the ordered accepted input prefix, or zero padding justified by an accepted frame end; readiness does not gate this safety check.
Every presented last flag identifies exactly the final retained or padded byte of its output frame.
Every presented header describes the next completed accepted input frame with correct original length, adjusted length, padding and truncation, independently of data-channel progress.
Blocked data and header channels independently preserve valid and payload through the next transfer opportunity; a reset edge cancels hold obligations.
Reset clears response valids and discards epoch state without erasing recorded failures. Unknown meaningful response controls or saved payloads cannot establish success.

The final-post marker combinationally enables completion checking: a qualifying drain tail, idle offers and responses, no partial accepted frame, and both independent response cursors fully drained are required, without another clock edge.

properties.description: Every presented data byte matches the ordered accepted input prefix or zero padding justified by an accepted frame end, regardless of output readiness.
Every presented last flag marks exactly the final retained or padded byte of its output frame, including streaming partial input prefixes.
Every presented header describes the next completed accepted input frame with correct original length, adjusted length, padding and truncation, independently of data-channel progress.
Blocked data and header channels independently preserve valid and payload until transfer or a reset edge.
Reset clears response valids and cancels epoch obligations without erasing recorded failures. Unknown meaningful response controls and payloads cannot establish success.

The final-post marker combinationally checks finite completion: a ready-high idle tail of at least 32 cycles, idle offers and responses, no partial accepted frame, and both response cursors drained. The tail counter accommodates the final workload's 128-cycle tail; no further edge is required.
